content.comment_body: Hi! I'm trying to create a program where a sensor normally controls output, but I want to add a manual control using the inputs i1 and i2. I've achieved the automatic part and included noise filters. I can't figure out how to manually override the sensor command. My goal is for two inputs: i1 should gradually increase the value (for example, if the sensor reads 450, pressing i1 should raise the value incrementally until i1 is released, then the value stays). Similarly, i2 should decrease the value in the same way. Additionally, a third input i3 should toggle between automatic and manual control (i3 = 0 enables automatic, i3 = 1 enables manual). I would appreciate guidance on how to add this manual control feature.

Hello, Please see the attached files for my proposed solution to your issue. The file "[document]" shows my demonstration of how it works. The file "[document]" integrates my solution with your circuit "[document]". If you have any questions, feel free to ask here. Best regards, [user_name]
Hi! I don't have any questions. Your example was very helpful. Thanks a lot.

analysis.insight_summary: The user wanted to implement manual override for an analog output, allowing gradual adjustment through digital inputs and switching modes between automatic and manual. By receiving an example project, the user achieved their goal. The exchange highlights how users appreciate practical, clear examples and flexible control logic.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects smooth manual adjustment of an analog output using specific inputs, for the current output to remain stable after input release, and for intuitive switching between automatic and manual operation using an extra input.
